mechanism_narrative: Sustained upward trend in GROCERY_PHARM mobility (0.1 → 3.6 over 4 weeks) signals normalization of essential shopping patterns. This normalization reduces friction for discretionary retail visits, causing RETAIL_REC to continue rising over the next 4 weeks as behavioral confidence in public spaces recovers.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM increased 3.5 percentage points over 4 weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over next 28 days does not exceed mean over prior 28 days, or GROCERY_PHARM reverses to negative territory in week t+1.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility remains persistently elevated (11.3–11.9) while RETAIL_REC shows consistent week-on-week improvement (-16.1 → -12.1). This decoupling indicates a shift in household time allocation: residents are gradually reallocating time from home to retail venues as confidence rebuilds, driving continued RETAIL_REC gains.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved 4.0 points while RESIDENTIAL remained stable
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility falls below 10.5 in any week t+1 to t+4, or RETAIL_REC reverses to decline in week t+1.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT station mobility has stabilized at -20.1 to -20.6 over the last 3 weeks, indicating a floor in commuting suppression. If TRANSIT remains above -21 for the next 2 weeks, this signals that commuting constraints are no longer tightening, allowing retail-adjacent foot traffic to normalize and RETAIL_REC to accelerate upward.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains above -21 percentage points for 2 consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT stabilized at -20.1 in week t-0w
failure_condition: TRANSIT falls below -21 in either of weeks t+1 or t+2, or RETAIL_REC declines in week t+1.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has stabilized near -9.7 (range -8.3 to -10.7 over 4 weeks), suggesting workplace capacity or attendance policies are no longer tightening. Stabilization of workplace suppression removes a drag on retail demand from commuters, allowing RETAIL_REC to continue its upward trajectory over the next 4 weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES variance < 2.5 percentage points over 2 consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES range is 2.4 points over 4 weeks
failure_condition: WORKPLACES falls more than 2 percentage points in any single week t+1 to t+4, or RETAIL_REC mean over next 28 days does not exceed prior 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has recovered from -15.0 to -10.7 over 4 weeks, indicating outdoor activity normalization. This outdoor mobility recovery precedes and enables retail recovery: as residents rebuild comfort in public spaces outdoors, they extend trips to include retail venues, driving RETAIL_REC higher over the next 4 weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS improves by > 1.5 percentage points in week t+1
failure_condition: PARKS reverses to decline in week t+1, or RETAIL_REC fails to improve in week t+1 despite PARKS improvement.

mechanism_narrative: The joint signal of TRANSIT stabilization (-20.1) and WORKPLACES stabilization (-9.7) indicates that commuting-suppression policies have reached a steady state. Under this regime, the marginal commuter can now plan retail trips with confidence, causing RETAIL_REC to accelerate upward over the next 2 weeks as trip-chaining behavior resumes.
candidate_trigger: both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain within ±1 percentage point of their t-0w values in week t+1
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at -20.1 and WORKPLACES at -9.7 in week t-0w
failure_condition: Either TRANSIT or WORKPLACES moves more than 1 percentage point in week t+1, or RETAIL_REC does not improve in week t+1.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has improved 4.0 percentage points over 4 weeks (-16.1 → -12.1) at a consistent rate (~1 point/week). Extrapolating this linear trend forward, RETAIL_REC will continue to improve at the same rate over the next 4 weeks, reaching approximately -8.1, thus remaining higher than the prior 4-week mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved 1.0 percentage point per week on average
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines in any week t+1 to t+4, or the 4-week mean over t+1 to t+4 is lower than the 4-week mean over t-3w to t-0w.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL elevation (11.3–11.9) combined with PARKS suppression (-10.7) indicates residents are confined indoors but increasingly willing to venture out. If PARKS mobility improves by > 2 percentage points in week t+1, this signals a behavioral shift toward outdoor activity that will cascade into retail venues within 1 week, causing RETAIL_REC to spike upward.
candidate_trigger: PARKS improves by > 2 percentage points in week t+1 relative to week t-0w
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS at -10.7 and RESIDENTIAL at 11.4 in week t-0w
failure_condition: PARKS does not improve by > 2 percentage points in week t+1, or RETAIL_REC does not improve in week t+1 despite PARKS improvement > 2 points.
